Former [[Governor of Alaska|Governor]] [[Sarah Palin]] did not run, having [[Resignation of Sarah Palin|resigned]] in July 2009.{{cite web | url = https://www.politico.com/story/2009/07/palin-announces-resignation-024497 | title =Palin announces resignation | publisher = Politico | author = Jonathan Martin}} Incumbent [[Governor of Alaska|Governor]] [[Sean Parnell]], who as [[List of lieutenant governors of Alaska|lieutenant governor]] succeeded Palin following her resignation, announced that he would seek a full term.{{cite web|url=http://www.ctvnews.ca/is-palin-retiring-or-running-for-president-in-2012-1.413694 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090706045916/http://www.ctv.ca/servlet/ArticleNews/story/CTVNews/20090704/palin_future_090704/20090704?hub=TopStories |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 6, 2009 |title=Is Palin retiring, or running for president in 2012? - CTV News |publisher=Ctv.ca |date=2009-07-04 |access-date=2010-08-21}} Following the primary election on Tuesday, August 24, 2010, the Democratic ticket consists of [[Ethan Berkowitz]] and [[Diane E. Benson]] running against Republican Parnell and his running mate, [[Mead Treadwell]].{{Cite web |url=http://www.adn.com/2010/08/24/1423340/lieutenant-govenor-candidates.html |title=Treadwell, Benson win lieutenant governor races |access-date=2010-09-13 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100828062653/http://www.adn.com/2010/08/24/1423340/lieutenant-govenor-candidates.html |archive-date=2010-08-28 |url-status=dead }} In the general election Parnell/Treadwell defeated Berkowitz/Benson by a wide margin.[http://aprn.org/2010/11/03/election-night-2010-incumbents-parnell-and-young-re-elected-possibly-murkowski/ Election Night 2010: Incumbents Parnell and Young Re-Elected, Possibly Murkowski] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101104151824/http://aprn.org/2010/11/03/election-night-2010-incumbents-parnell-and-young-re-elected-possibly-murkowski/ |date=November 4, 2010 }}, [[Alaska Public Radio Network|APRN]] 3-10-2010 Parnell received just over 59% of the vote, the highest percentage for any Alaska gubernatorial candidate in history. This is the only election in Alaskan history where any party won three consecutive gubernatorial elections.{{Cite web |title=GEMS ELECTION RESULTS |url=https://www.elections.alaska.gov/Core/Archive/10GENR/data/resultsOF.htm |access-date=2026-09-27 |website=www.elections.alaska.gov}} ==Republican primary== ===Certified for the ballot=== * Gerald L.
